title: Airbags and Seatbelt Pretensioners: SRS Component Locations
introduction:
I read these drawings like a seating chart for the supplemental restraint system: they show where the information-gathering components sit and where the deployable restraints are positioned. The seat belts and SRS work together, while the restraints controller uses sensor and occupant information to coordinate the response. Finding a component on the map is useful; it does not tell us that component is faulty.

### Read the sensing and control map

In the first drawing, follow the line from each enlarged component to its highlighted position in the transparent body. The RCM is the restraints control module, shown in the central floor area. The OCSM is the occupant classification system module associated with the passenger-seat sensing arrangement; OCS means occupant classification system. The overhead-console reference includes the PAD indicator, meaning passenger airbag deactivation. These labels connect the physical map to the system's control and occupant-information functions.

The front-body, door, seat and steering-column locations give useful landmarks. They do not show how to uncover those parts. Read the description beside the callout carefully: an assembly entry can include sensing hardware that would be easy to overlook if you judged only by its outer shape.

### Read the restraint map

The other drawing locates belt assemblies and deployable components around the seats, roof, steering wheel and instrument panel. Its callout sequence is independent of the first drawing, so always use the table beside the illustration you are viewing.

This view combines body-style alternatives. Coupe-only roof curtains and convertible-only upper side airbags must be read with their qualifiers; the drawing is not a checklist of equipment fitted simultaneously to every Mustang. Likewise, retain the driver/passenger and steering-side qualifications when matching a location to the car.

These are component-location references. They provide no physical access, depowering, connector-probing, diagnostic-test, removal or restoration sequence.

items.name: Qualified personnel and dedicated restraint procedures
items.detail: Pyrotechnic-component service is restricted to qualified personnel. Any service requires the dedicated SRS depowering, handling, testing and restoration procedures and specified equipment. This location map does not replace them; do not substitute a generic jumper or resistance test.

edits.text: NOTE: A left-hand-drive (LHD) vehicle is shown; the right-hand-drive (RHD) arrangement is similar.
edits.why: Similar does not mean that every driver/passenger label carries across unchanged. Use the LHD/RHD alternatives in the adjoining table when identifying the door and front impact sensors.
